answer: Divergent History Passports. Each identity carries a signed, append-only history of its interactions; before any new action, the agent must present a fresh proof derived from that history. Clones share identical records, so they cannot produce distinct proofs without forking state. The network acts as a haven for honest agents, since only one branch per history is accepted. An attacker must physically diverge each clone across a river of separate transaction histories, and every fork crossing costs a full synchronization round that must be maintained at a harbor of verified checkpoints.
